This is the first of fifteen Psalms (Psalms 120-134) entitled "A Song of Degrees" (<reference osisRef="Ps.121.1">Psa 121:1</reference>--literally, "A song for the degrees"), or ascents. It seems most probable they were designed for the use of the people when going up (compare <reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.27">1Ki 12:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.28">28</reference>) to Jerusalem on the festival occasions (<reference osisRef="Deut.16.16">De 16:16</reference>), three times a year. David appears as the author of four, Solomon of one (<reference osisRef="Ps.127.1">Psa 127:1</reference>), and the other ten are anonymous, probably composed after the captivity. In this Psalm the writer acknowledges God's mercy, prays for relief from a malicious foe, whose punishment he anticipates, and then repeats his complaint.</title> <div sID="gen10717" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6981"/>2-3.
